description: The 3-D Animation in Cinematic Arts Minor offers students an opportunity to learn a broad range of skills and techniques related to 3-D computer animation. The goal of the minor is to foster talented artists and animators to create compelling animation, from conceptualization to modeling, rigging, animation and rendering. The minor is a useful supplement to a wide array of majors, from those within the cinematic arts, such as visual effects, animation and games, to those within engineering, such as computer science, and to majors within the fine arts, such as painting, drawing and photography, and beyond. This minor is not available to students in the BA in Animation and Digital Arts, the BFA in Animation and Digital Arts or the BS in Computer Science (Games) programs.

The minor in 3-Dimensional Design teaches the language of form as a foundation for understanding the aesthetic, functional and structural concerns of three-dimensional objects and spaces. Through a range of projects and media, students develop skills in observation, conceptualization, and representation of 3-D forms in both physical and digital modes. The minor also provides an opportunity to develop an understanding of the relationship of 3-D design to its history and to the larger contexts of art and society.

The Accounting Minor is designed for students outside of the Leventhal School of Accounting who desire an understanding of the concepts and principles of accounting. This minor provides a foundational knowledge of accounting crucial for understanding business operations and financial health. Students will gain insights into financial reporting, managerial accounting, and the role of accounting information in decision-making, equipping them with valuable skills applicable across various industries and professions.
Accreditation status: The Marshall School of Business and Leventhal School of Accounting are accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description: The Addiction Science minor is designed for students interested in a career in public health, health care, social work, public policy, or medicine, with a particular focus on addiction and related issues. Students learn to recognize substance use disorders and addictive behaviors in various populations, how to implement evidence-based screening and prevention strategies across diverse settings, and develop a foundational understanding of the biological, psychological, and sociological underpinnings of addiction. Students also examine the role of public policy, epidemiology, and health services in addressing addiction and health equity. Graduates will gain expertise in addressing this critical public health issue from multiple perspectives and will be equipped to make a meaningful impact in their chosen professional path.

The Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism offers an interdisciplinary minor in advertising that prepares students for careers in the dynamic field of advertising. The minor introduces students to the principles and practices of advertising through a blend of courses in communication, business, and design. Students learn about advertising strategy, media planning, creative development, and consumer insights, gaining a comprehensive understanding of the advertising industry. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical knowledge and practical skills, preparing students to develop effective advertising campaigns in a rapidly evolving media landscape.
A dynamic interdisciplinary major focused on the experiences, history, culture, and intellectual traditions of African peoples throughout the world.

This interdisciplinary minor introduces students to the study of race and ethnicity in the United States and the Americas. The program encourages students to analyze the history and contemporary experience of racial and ethnic groups in the United States, and to consider the theoretical, political, and cultural implications of race and ethnicity as categories of analysis in American society. Students will develop an understanding of various historical periods, cultural forms, and social movements, as well as the interplay of race, gender, class, and sexuality. Course work can include topics such as Native American studies, African American studies, Asian American studies, Chicano/Latino studies, and comparative ethnic studies.

The Ph.D. program in Anthropology (Visual Anthropology) at the University of Southern California has been in existence since 1983. It is designed to train students in the analysis of visual systems and the production of visual media, including ethnographic film, photography, and new media. It is unique in its integration of theoretical training in anthropology with professional training in ethnographic media production. Visual anthropology focuses on the study of culture through visual modalities (e.g. ethnographic film, photography, new media, performance, architecture, the built environment) and, relatedly, on the study of how people communicate through such media, and how anthropologists might represent culture using them. In keeping with this, faculty in visual anthropology teach and train students in critical approaches to analyzing and making visual media, and in using visual media to communicate ethnographic knowledge and theory. We train students in theory, methods, and the history of visual anthropology; they produce a visual ethnographic project in addition to a written dissertation. The program encourages interdisciplinary work with other departments at USC, including Cinema, Art History, and American Studies and Ethnicity.

The minor in Asian American Studies introduces students to the experiences of Asian Americans through an interdisciplinary approach that considers issues of race, gender, sexuality, ethnicity, and class in historical and contemporary contexts. The minor aims to provide students with a critical understanding of the forces that have shaped Asian American communities and how Asian Americans have responded to and resisted these forces. The minor prepares students to engage with a diverse society and to become advocates for social justice.

A growing body of research suggests that psychological factors influence economic behavior, decision-making, and market outcomes. The minor in Behavioral Economics and Psychology introduces students to foundational knowledge in both fields as they relate to and integrate with one another. Students will gain an understanding of the cognitive, social, and emotional factors that influence individual decision-making, as well as an understanding of how these factors can lead to deviations from traditional economic models. The minor provides students with an interdisciplinary perspective on human behavior, equipping them with valuable analytical tools applicable to various fields, including public policy, marketing, finance, and organizational behavior.

The Biophysics program is housed in the Department of Biological Sciences. It is an interdisciplinary program designed to train students for careers in biophysics research. The program emphasizes the application of quantitative approaches to biological problems and provides students with a strong foundation in physics, mathematics, and biology, as well as hands-on research experience.

The Central European Studies minor provides students with an understanding of Central Europe (Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary) from a multidisciplinary perspective, including literature, film, history, political science and culture. Students will learn about the region’s rich history and complex present and gain an understanding of its important role in contemporary Europe.

The Chicano/Latino Studies program offers an interdisciplinary curriculum that explores the experiences of Chicana/os and Latina/os in the United States and transnational contexts. Students examine the historical, political, social, economic, and cultural forces that have shaped and continue to shape Chicana/o and Latina/o communities. The program offers a broad understanding of Chicana/o and Latina/o communities from a comparative, critical, and interdisciplinary perspective. The BA in Chicano/Latino Studies is ideal for students interested in careers in law, public policy, education, social work, journalism, and community organizing, as well as those pursuing graduate studies in the humanities and social sciences. Students develop critical thinking, analytical, and communication skills, preparing them to address complex social issues and contribute to diverse communities.

The minor in computational linguistics, offered jointly by the Department of Linguistics and the Department of Computer Science, focuses on theoretical and practical aspects of language technology. The program provides students with a solid background in both linguistics and computer science and prepares them for further study or entry-level positions in areas such as natural language processing, information retrieval, machine translation, and speech recognition.

The PhD in Computational Neuroscience is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a broad background in theoretical and computational approaches to neuroscience. Students will develop a strong foundation in the mathematical and computational tools necessary to understand the brain's complex functions, from the molecular and cellular level to systems and cognitive processes. The program emphasizes both theoretical understanding and practical application, preparing graduates for research careers in academia or industry.

The minor in Contemporary Latino and Latin American Studies provides students with an interdisciplinary understanding of the historical, social, political, economic and cultural experiences of Latina/os in the United States, as well as those of peoples and nations throughout Latin America and the Caribbean. The minor allows students to apply the analytical tools and perspectives of the humanities and social sciences to the study of a vibrant and increasingly influential demographic in the United States, and to explore the challenges and opportunities for transnational exchange and collaboration with Latin American societies. The minor also helps students prepare for graduate work in area studies or related fields such as sociology, political science, history, literature and anthropology, as well as for careers in public policy, government, law, education, business, journalism, social work, and community organizing.
Program name: Contemporary Latino and Latin American Studies

description: The Data Science program provides graduate students with the interdisciplinary knowledge and skills needed to manage and analyze large datasets. Students will develop a strong foundation in areas such as machine learning, data mining, statistical modeling, and data visualization. The program emphasizes both theoretical understanding and practical application, preparing graduates for careers in diverse fields including technology, finance, healthcare, and research.

The Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Data Science is an interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers that require both economic analysis and data science skills. This program provides students with a strong foundation in economic theory and quantitative methods, as well as the computational and statistical skills necessary to analyze large datasets. Students will learn how to apply economic principles to real-world problems using modern data science techniques, including machine learning, econometrics, and data visualization. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and the ethical considerations of data analysis. Upon completion of the Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Data Science, students will be able to: Demonstrate a strong understanding of economic theory and quantitative methods. Apply data science techniques to analyze economic data, including machine learning and econometrics. Communicate economic insights effectively through data visualization and written reports. Evaluate the ethical implications of data collection and analysis.

The Bachelor of Arts in Economics/Mathematics offers students the opportunity to combine serious study in both disciplines. Students interested in quantitative approaches to economics and economic theory, as well as those planning to pursue graduate study in economics, mathematics or related fields, will find this major particularly appropriate. The Economics/Mathematics curriculum is designed to provide students with: 1. A solid foundation in microeconomics and macroeconomics. 2. A strong foundation in mathematical methods. 3. An understanding of statistics and econometrics and their applications. 4. The ability to use quantitative methods to analyze economic problems. 5. Critical thinking and problem-solving skills.

Students in the Environmental Science and Health major examine the scientific basis of environmental problems and their impact on human health. They gain a solid foundation in environmental chemistry, earth sciences, life sciences and quantitative methods, as well as an understanding of the social and public policy aspects of environmental problems and human health. The major emphasizes quantitative and analytical skills and prepares students for careers or graduate study in environmental science, environmental health, public health, environmental consulting, and environmental policy and law.

The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Film & Television Production is an intensive program of study in the theory and practice of producing, directing, writing, cinematography, editing, sound, and interactive media. Students gain experience through the creation of a range of projects from traditional narratives and documentaries to interactive and experimental forms. Emphasis is placed on collaboration and creative leadership throughout the filmmaking process. The program develops filmmakers who are original storytellers capable of working across all mediums. Upon graduation, students have a portfolio of work and the skills to enter the film and television industry.

Undergraduate instruction in French is designed to acquaint students with the language, literatures, and cultures of France and the French-speaking world. In addition to language training, course work covers French and Francophone literatures and cultures, literary and critical theory, film, history, and the history of ideas. Students develop skills in critical analysis, analytical and argumentative writing, and oral expression.

A joint major is offered in French and Italian. A total of 32 units beyond French 200 or 220 and Italian 200 or 220 are required. Students must complete 16 units in French beyond French 200 or 220, including French 300, 320 and 370. They must also complete 16 units in Italian beyond Italian 200 or 220, including Italian 300, 320 and 370.

The Bachelor of Arts in Gender and Sexuality Studies provides students with the opportunity to pursue an interdisciplinary course of study that examines the intersections of gender, sexuality, race, class, religion, and nation in diverse global and historical contexts. Through an exploration of cutting-edge scholarship, students develop analytical skills and critical perspectives on social justice issues, preparing them for careers in fields such as law, education, public policy, health, social work, journalism, and the arts, as well as for graduate study. This program offers students an opportunity to explore a variety of methods and approaches to feminist and queer scholarship, with a particular strength in transnational and postcolonial feminist approaches. A unique strength of the program is its integration of theory and practice through community-based learning opportunities in Los Angeles. The GSS BA also emphasizes the interdisciplinary nature of the field by allowing students to complete coursework in other departments.

The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Geological Sciences requires a minimum of 60 units of graduate work beyond the bachelor’s degree, or 48 units beyond the master’s degree. Students are encouraged to pursue an individualized program of study in consultation with their faculty adviser. The degree prepares students for research and teaching careers in academia or research careers in industry or government. Students must choose an area of specialization from those listed below under Areas of Study. Students may take courses from other departments when appropriate. A qualifying exam, a dissertation proposal and a dissertation defense are required. Teaching assistantships are a normal part of the PhD training. Requirements for the PhD degree are intended to be completed in four to five years, though the time will vary from student to student.

The USC Global Geodesign graduate certificate is designed to provide professional training for students and practitioners who are working to understand and analyze complex environmental and social issues to propose design solutions that address these challenges locally and globally. Geodesign is an emerging practice that bridges geographic information systems (GIS) and planning and design in an interactive process, integrating geographic science and analysis with design practice, providing an iterative workflow that uses scientific information to inform design proposals. The 12-unit certificate is an interdisciplinary program that draws from the fields of spatial sciences, landscape architecture, and urban planning. The certificate is offered primarily online, with an optional one-week, in-person design charrette studio at the end of the summer session.

The minor in Health and Humanity focuses on the social, cultural, and historical dimensions of health and healing. The program introduces students to critical approaches to the study of health and medicine, and prepares them to understand the diverse ways that different societies and cultures define, understand, and address issues of health and disease. Through the minor, students learn to contextualize contemporary health challenges, to appreciate the variety of medical traditions, and to understand the role of healing in human society. The minor draws on the insights and methods of a wide range of humanistic and social science disciplines, including anthropology, history, literature, philosophy, psychology, religious studies, and sociology. The minor is a valuable complement to majors in the natural sciences, public health, and other health-related fields, as well as to majors in the humanities and social sciences. The minor also helps prepare students for careers in health care, public health, health policy, and related fields.

The Bachelor of Science in Health and Human Sciences provides a scientific and interdisciplinary foundation for students interested in careers related to health, human behavior and the human body. The curriculum emphasizes the biological, behavioral and social sciences, and prepares students for a wide variety of entry-level positions in health-related fields, or for further graduate or professional training.

The Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) with a concentration in History and Social Science provides initial preparation for individuals seeking a California preliminary single subject teaching credential in History and Social Science. The USC Rossier School of Education offers this program. This program leads to a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Urban Education with a specialization in History and Social Science Education. This is an advanced degree for students who intend to pursue research careers as university faculty or in applied research organizations.

Human Biology is the study of human life, incorporating knowledge from the biological and social sciences. The major emphasizes an evolutionary perspective on human biology, considering the origins and ramifications of human biological variation, adaptation, and behavior. The curriculum provides students with a strong background in general biology, human anatomy and physiology, genetics, development, ecology and evolution, and behavior. Graduates of the program will have a broad understanding of the scientific study of human biology, from genes to global populations, and are well prepared for careers in health professions, science, education, public health, and conservation, as well as graduate study in related fields.

Description and Learning Objectives:
Upon completion of the Human Biology BA program, students will be able to:
* Explain the basic principles of evolution and how they apply to human biology, behavior, and culture.
* Apply an understanding of human genetics, development, anatomy, and physiology to explain the function and variation of the human body.
* Explain the social, cultural, and ecological factors that influence human health, disease, and behavior.
* Evaluate scientific literature, analyze data, and communicate scientific findings effectively in both written and oral forms.
* Understand the ethical implications of biological research and its application to human society.

The Master of Science in Human Security and Geospatial Intelligence (HSGI) provides students with knowledge and analytic capabilities to address critical issues related to human security, humanitarian intervention, and the uses of geospatial intelligence in these efforts. The interdisciplinary curriculum integrates the study of human security with geospatial intelligence concepts, tools, and practices, preparing students for careers in diverse sectors, including national and international government agencies, non-governmental organizations, and private companies.

The Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering provides an education that will prepare students to address the design and improvement of complex systems. The discipline uses mathematical, physical and social sciences together with engineering analysis and design to specify, predict and evaluate the results to be obtained from such systems. Emphasis is placed on the integration of people, materials, information, equipment and energy. Industrial and systems engineers work with technology, information and management in manufacturing and service industries. Students are required to take a minimum of 128 units.

The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree in Intelligence and Cyber Operations is a rigorous, interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers in the intelligence community and various cyber operations roles within both government and the private sector. This program integrates a unique blend of technical skills, analytical methods, and strategic understanding, positioning graduates at the forefront of national security and cybersecurity challenges. The curriculum emphasizes foundational knowledge in computer science, cybersecurity, data analysis, and intelligence studies, coupled with practical training in ethical hacking, digital forensics, and threat intelligence. Students will develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills essential for effective performance in complex and rapidly evolving operational environments. Graduates will be equipped to tackle multifaceted challenges related to cyber espionage, counterterrorism, information warfare, and critical infrastructure protection.

The International Relations (Global Business) major provides students with a detailed understanding of the international political economy. It focuses on the political dynamics of international trade, finance, and business, as well as foreign policy, regional security, and international law and organization. The curriculum blends the strengths of USC Dornsife College’s International Relations program with USC Marshall School of Business’s expertise in global business. Students study political and economic theories, examine the global economic system through an international relations lens, and gain analytical skills necessary to evaluate the international business environment.

This major provides a comprehensive understanding of the international political economy, with an emphasis on the interaction between economic and political processes in a global context. It examines the major theories and current issues in international political economy, international trade, international finance, and economic development. Students pursuing this major will develop a strong analytical foundation for understanding global issues from an interdisciplinary perspective. The major prepares students for graduate studies in international relations, economics, business, and law, as well as for careers in international business, banking and finance, journalism, consulting, and government and non-governmental organizations.
Program name: International Relations and the Global Economy

description: A minor in Italian allows students to gain proficiency in the Italian language and to study the literature and culture of Italy. Students must complete 20 units of coursework with a grade of C or better. A minimum of 20 units above ITAL 120, including a minimum of 8 units at the 300 level or above, is required for the minor.

The minor in Jewish Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a comprehensive knowledge of the history, culture and religion of the Jewish people and Judaism. Students are exposed to a broad range of courses, from literature, history, religion and philosophy to sociology, political science and modern Hebrew language, and participate in academic and cultural events.

The major in Latin American and Iberian Cultures offers an interdisciplinary approach to the cultures, literatures and civilizations of Latin America, Spain, Portugal and other Portuguese-speaking countries, and to the study of the Spanish and Portuguese languages. Students majoring in Latin American and Iberian Cultures are encouraged to study abroad in one of the approved programs in Latin America or Spain for one or two semesters. Contact the study abroad office (Doheny Memorial Library, DML 104) for a list of approved programs.

The minor in Latin American and Iberian Cultures, Media and Politics offers students an interdisciplinary approach to the study of the cultures, media and politics of Latin America and the Iberian Peninsula (Spain and Portugal). The minor provides an opportunity to combine courses from areas such as Spanish, Portuguese, Latin American and Iberian Studies, Cinematic Arts, Political Science, International Relations, History, and Anthropology. Students will gain a deep understanding of the diverse histories, cultures, media, and political landscapes of these regions, while also enhancing their language skills (Spanish or Portuguese). The minor culminates in a capstone experience where students apply their knowledge to a specific research project, internship, or study abroad experience in the region.
Program name: Latin American and Iberian Cultures, Media and Politics

description: The minor in Law, History and Culture offers an interdisciplinary approach to the study of law, legal systems, and legal cultures from a humanities perspective. It provides students with critical insight into the historical development of law, legal institutions and legal theory, and with a nuanced understanding of the cultural and social effects of law. It also enables students to develop skills in the historical analysis of primary documents, and in the critical interpretation of legal texts and judicial opinions. The minor is a valuable complement to a variety of majors including international relations, political science, history, sociology, philosophy, and gender studies. The minor also provides an excellent basis for students considering graduate study in law or in the humanities. The Law, History and Culture minor is offered by the Department of History.

Materials Science (MSCI) is an interdisciplinary field, drawing on the disciplines of physics, chemistry and engineering to understand the fundamental relationships between the processing, structure and properties of materials. This understanding is used to design new materials and to improve the performance of existing ones. Materials are a ubiquitous enabling technology for fields ranging from quantum computing to space exploration, and materials scientists are critical to solving grand challenges in energy, health, infrastructure, and sustainability. The Department of Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering offers programs of graduate study leading to the Master of Science (MS) in Materials Science and the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Materials Science.

The Queer Arts and Culture Minor is designed for students interested in exploring the role of arts and culture in the formation of queer identities, communities, and social movements. This minor offers an interdisciplinary approach to studying the intersections of LGBTQ+ experiences with various artistic forms, cultural practices, and media. Students will engage with critical theories and historical perspectives to understand how queer artists and cultural producers have challenged norms, expressed dissent, and forged new ways of being and relating. The curriculum covers a range of topics including queer performance, film, literature, visual arts, and digital culture, encouraging students to analyze cultural texts and practices through a queer lens. The minor aims to foster analytical skills, creative thinking, and a deeper appreciation for the contributions of queer artists and cultural workers to broader society.

The minor in Race, Ethnicity, and Politics exposes students to the political study of race and ethnicity, especially the way in which race and ethnicity shape the behavior of political actors, political institutions, and political systems. The minor examines race and ethnicity in both American and comparative political contexts and provides students with a set of tools to analyze critically the role of race and ethnicity in political life.

The Department of Religion offers courses on the major religious traditions of the world — Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, and Judaism — as well as on new religious movements and on ancient, indigenous, and non-Western religions. Courses address religion from a variety of disciplinary perspectives, including anthropology, critical theory, history, literary studies, philosophy, and sociology. Students learn to analyze and understand religious phenomena in diverse cultural and historical contexts and to evaluate critically the role of religion in human society, both past and present. Majors are trained in critical thinking, the analysis of complex cultural systems, and sophisticated expository writing.

This minor draws on the faculty and courses of a number of departments and programs to provide undergraduates with an interdisciplinary understanding of the period of the Renaissance, Early Modern, and Reformation eras (roughly 1400-1800). This period is one of extraordinary dynamism and change, which gave birth to many of the ideas, institutions, and practices of the modern world, as well as forms of cultural and aesthetic expression still vibrant today. Courses available will address the religious upheavals of the Reformation; the scientific revolution; the impact of the printing press; the rise of the nation-state and the international legal order; the development of the global economy and colonialism; the rise of capitalism; changes in gender and family structures; developments in art, architecture, music, and literary forms; and the impact of these developments on philosophy and political thought. Students completing the minor will emerge with a sophisticated understanding of the historical roots of many contemporary issues and problems, as well as a deeper appreciation of the complex cultural heritage that shapes our lives.
Program name: Renaissance, Early Modern, and Reformation Studies Minor

description: The minor in Russian introduces students to a major language, literature and culture of the world through coursework in Russian language, literature and culture. It is an excellent complement to majors in the humanities and social sciences. The minor also provides an excellent foundation for professional careers in government, journalism, international relations and law, and for graduate work in Russian or other fields.

The minor in Science, Technology, and Society (STS) gives students an interdisciplinary education in the ways that science and technology shape society and culture, and the ways that society and culture shape science and technology. Students in the minor will learn how to critically examine the assumptions, practices, and products of scientific and technological endeavors. The STS minor is structured to provide students with a solid intellectual foundation in the history, philosophy, and sociology of science and technology. Students will also learn to analyze scientific and technological controversies and the ethical, legal, political, and cultural aspects of scientific knowledge production and technological development. STS minors will also gain an understanding of science communication and the roles of expertise and publics in a democratic society.

The Spanish minor introduces students to the language, culture, and civilization of the Spanish-speaking world. The minor improves students’ linguistic competency and expands their understanding of Spanish and Latin American cultures, which prepares them for a variety of professions in a global context.

The Thematic Approaches to Culture minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a comprehensive understanding of human culture from various disciplinary perspectives. Through a flexible curriculum, students will explore cultural phenomena, expressions, and practices across different historical periods and geographical regions. The program aims to equip students with the analytical tools necessary to critically engage with diverse cultural forms, including literature, art, media, religion, and social movements. Students will develop critical thinking and research skills, learn to analyze cultural phenomena from multiple perspectives, and communicate their insights effectively. The minor is suitable for students from any major interested in deepening their understanding of the complexities of human culture.

The Visual Culture Minor introduces students to the study of visuality as a central aspect of human experience. Drawing on a range of disciplinary perspectives—art history, critical theory, literature, media studies, performance studies, philosophy—the minor explores the social and cultural significance of images and visual practices across different historical periods and geographical locations. Students will develop critical tools to analyze how visual culture shapes identities, knowledge, power relations, and various forms of expression, from fine art and popular culture to digital media and scientific imaging. The curriculum emphasizes interdisciplinary approaches, encouraging students to engage with diverse visual forms and theoretical frameworks. Through coursework, students will enhance their ability to interpret complex visual phenomena, articulate informed arguments, and contribute to contemporary debates about the role of the visual in society.

The Web Technologies and Applications minor provides students with the fundamental knowledge and skills needed to design, develop, and deploy modern web-based applications. The minor emphasizes both the client-side (front-end) and server-side (back-end) aspects of web development, covering topics such as user interface design, web programming languages, database integration, and web security. Students will gain practical experience through hands-on projects, preparing them for careers in web development, software engineering, and related fields.

The Bachelor of Science in Accounting is designed for students who are committed to a career in accounting. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in all areas of accounting, including financial accounting, managerial accounting, auditing, and taxation. Students also gain a broader understanding of business principles through courses in finance, marketing, and management. The program prepares graduates for entry-level positions in public accounting, corporate accounting, government, and non-profit organizations. It also provides an excellent foundation for pursuing graduate studies in accounting or related fields, such as law or business.

The Bachelor of Science in Accounting and Finance is a limited enrollment program designed to provide students with a strong foundation in both disciplines, preparing them for careers that require an integrated understanding of accounting and finance. This joint program, offered by the Leventhal School of Accounting and the Department of Finance and Business Economics, provides students with rigorous training in financial reporting, corporate finance, investments, and financial analysis. Graduates are well-prepared for roles in investment banking, corporate finance, asset management, and public accounting, as well as for further graduate studies.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Accounting and Finance

description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Acting, Stage and Screen program is a highly selective conservatory-style program designed for students seeking rigorous training in the craft of acting for theatre, film, and television. Students will develop a comprehensive set of acting skills, including voice, movement, scene study, improvisation, and script analysis. The curriculum also integrates foundational knowledge in theatre history, dramatic literature, and professional practices. Graduates will be prepared to pursue careers as professional actors in various media, equipped with a versatile skill set and a deep understanding of the acting profession.
Program name: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Acting, Stage and Screen

description: The Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering is offered by the Department of Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in engineering principles and prepares students to analyze, design, and operate aerospace systems. Course work includes an introduction to the different fields of aerospace engineering, such as aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, flight mechanics and orbital mechanics, and includes design projects that give students hands-on experience in aerospace system development. The curriculum also includes courses in mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer programming, materials science, electrical engineering, and manufacturing. The aerospace engineering curriculum prepares students for careers in the aerospace industry, government laboratories, and for graduate studies in aerospace engineering. The program also provides a good foundation for careers in other fields, such as automotive, energy, and biomedical engineering. The program prepares students to attain the following educational objectives: (1) Our graduates will establish themselves as successful engineers in industry, government, or other professional careers by demonstrating technical proficiency, communication skills, and responsible teamwork. (2) Our graduates will be able to engage in continued learning and professional development.
Accreditation status: All undergraduate degree programs in engineering are accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, 111 Market Place, Suite 1050, Baltimore, MD 21202-4012; telephone 410-347-7700.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering

description: This interdisciplinary program gives students an opportunity to explore the historical contexts, theoretical issues, critical methods, and cultural forms that constitute American popular culture. Through courses from a number of different departments, students are encouraged to consider popular culture in relation to high culture; to examine the specific qualities of various popular culture genres, forms, and media; to develop critical skills in analyzing popular culture; and to develop an understanding of popular culture’s role in shaping individual and social identities. The program provides an excellent foundation for careers in the entertainment and communications industries, public relations, arts management, teaching, and law, as well as for further graduate study in a variety of fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in American Popular Culture

description: The Bachelor of Science in Medical Laboratory Science (MLS) program prepares students for a career in the medical laboratory field. The program provides students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences and professional courses in clinical laboratory disciplines. Students gain expertise in performing diagnostic laboratory tests in areas such as clinical chemistry, hematology, immunology, microbiology, transfusion medicine, and molecular diagnostics. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and quality assurance in the clinical laboratory setting. Students will also learn about laboratory operations, management, and ethical responsibilities. The program includes extensive hands-on laboratory experience and supervised clinical rotations in affiliated hospitals and clinical laboratories. Graduates are prepared for entry-level positions as medical laboratory scientists in various healthcare settings, including hospitals, clinics, public health laboratories, and research facilities. Students who successfully complete the program are eligible to take national certification examinations in medical laboratory science.
Accreditation status: The MLS program is accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Sciences (NAACLS), 5600 N. River Rd., Suite 720, Rosemont, IL 60018-5119; (773) 714-8880.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Medical Laboratory Science
Bachelor of Arts in Narrative Studies

description: The Bachelor of Science in Neuroscience (BS) program at USC is an interdepartmental program that provides a rigorous and broad education in neuroscience. Administered through the Neuroscience Graduate Program, the BS program combines strong foundations in biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics with a multidisciplinary understanding of brain function. Students are provided with hands-on research experience and opportunities to explore the various facets of neuroscience, from molecular and cellular mechanisms to systems and cognitive processes.

The Bachelor of Arts in Public Policy is a multidisciplinary major that provides students with a strong foundation in political science, economics, policy analysis and quantitative methods. Students gain the analytical, communication, and leadership skills necessary to address complex societal challenges and make a positive impact through public service. The curriculum integrates theoretical knowledge with practical applications, preparing students for a variety of careers in government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector, as well as for graduate studies in public policy, law, and related fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Public Policy

description: The Bachelor of Science in Quantitative Biology program is designed for students interested in combining a strong foundation in biology with a rigorous training in mathematics, statistics, computer science, and data analysis. The curriculum provides students with the quantitative skills necessary to address complex biological problems, from molecular to ecological scales. Graduates will be prepared for careers in research, biotechnology, computational biology, and further graduate studies in quantitative biology, bioinformatics, biostatistics, and related fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Quantitative Biology

description: The Bachelor of Science in Real Estate Development is a four-year professional degree program designed for students seeking to enter the field of real estate development. The undergraduate curriculum provides a strong background in the analytical and practical skills necessary to perform as a real estate development professional. The program encompasses both the private sector market-driven activities of property development, finance and management, and the public sector concerns for quality urban environments, economic development, community planning and infrastructure development. The curriculum provides a foundation in critical thinking, writing and oral presentation skills, as well as a solid understanding of market and economic analysis, regulatory review, finance, accounting and investment. Elective opportunities provide the student with flexibility in pursuing a particular area of interest in real estate development.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Real Estate Development

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Spatial Sciences (BA) offers students the opportunity to integrate an understanding of how spatial analysis and visualization technologies contribute to the creation of new knowledge in diverse fields of inquiry with a firm grounding in the liberal arts tradition. The curriculum provides core knowledge and skills in geographic information science and spatial data analysis, geographic information systems, remote sensing, and geodesy necessary for students to analyze complex geospatial data and derive meaningful information. Students may choose to use these core skills for an academic emphasis in either natural science or social science, complementing other course work in traditional disciplines such as geology, environmental studies, archaeology, political science, sociology, economics, or public policy. The BA in Spatial Sciences is an appropriate degree for students who want a grounding in spatial methods but intend to apply them as an integral part of another field of study such as international relations, journalism, urban planning, or business. This program may also be a good choice for students interested in graduate studies in a related field such as urban planning, public policy, public health, landscape architecture, business administration, political science, or communications. Students in the BA in Spatial Sciences are strongly encouraged to consider a minor or a second major in an area of their disciplinary interest.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Spatial Sciences

description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Spatial Sciences offers a comprehensive foundation in spatial theory, methods, and applications. Students develop expertise in geographic information science and technology (GIS&T) and gain practical skills in data acquisition, management, analysis, visualization, and communication, including experience with cutting-edge spatial software, big data, artificial intelligence, and virtual and augmented reality applications. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and ethical considerations related to spatial data. Graduates are prepared for diverse careers in fields such as environmental science, urban planning, public health, business, and national security, or for further graduate studies.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Spatial Sciences

Concentration name: Emphasis in Design, Emphasis in Stage Management
description: The BA in Theatre program offers a broad-based, liberal arts approach to the study of theatre. Designed for students who wish to pursue a major in theatre within the context of a strong general education, the program encourages students to develop skills in various aspects of theatre, including performance, dramatic literature, history, theory, and design. The program encourages students to explore multiple facets of theatre and potentially combine their studies with a minor or second major in another field. The program prepares students for a wide range of careers in the arts and other fields that value creative problem-solving, critical thinking, and collaborative skills.

The Bachelor in Adult Development, Gerontology, and Aging is designed for students who want to develop an understanding of the aging process from a multidisciplinary perspective. The program emphasizes both biological and social science approaches to the study of adult development and aging. Students in this program will learn about the social, psychological, biological, and economic aspects of aging, and how these factors impact individuals and society. The curriculum prepares students for careers in gerontology and related fields, such as health care, social services, public policy, and research. It also provides a strong foundation for graduate studies in gerontology or other related disciplines.
Program name: Bachelor in Adult Development, Gerontology, and Aging

description: The major in African American Studies provides an interdisciplinary approach to the study of people of African descent in the Americas and their global impact, with a particular focus on the United States and the Black Atlantic. This major introduces students to the theories and methods of the study of race and ethnicity, and trains them to engage critically in the analysis of power, inequality, and resistance. Coursework enables students to develop strong research, analytical, and communication skills, which are essential for careers in diverse fields, including education, public policy, community organizing, public health, social work, law, journalism, communications, and the arts.

Anthropology is the comparative study of human biological and cultural diversity across space and time. Anthropologists examine human origins and evolution, how humans adapt to different environments, and how they create meaning through language, art, ritual, and religion. Our undergraduate curriculum in Anthropology provides a comprehensive introduction to all four subfields of anthropology – sociocultural anthropology, linguistic anthropology, archaeological anthropology, and biological anthropology – with a particular emphasis on theoretical issues and the role of ethnographic, archaeological, and biological fieldwork. The Anthropology program prepares students for a wide range of careers. The major will give students an excellent foundation in human diversity and cross-cultural understanding, valuable for today’s globalized world. Many students choose to pursue graduate studies in Anthropology (cultural, biological, and archaeology), Public Health, Medical Anthropology, Law, International Relations, Education, or Journalism. Other students use their degrees to begin careers in government, non-profits, museums, international NGOs, forensic science, advertising, marketing, public relations, and business, or to enter the health professions. Our unique curriculum combines intellectual rigor with flexibility, allowing students to tailor their programs according to their interests while providing them with the necessary skills to be successful.

The archaeology program provides undergraduates with the opportunity to study the past through its material remains and learn methods and theories that are broadly applicable to a range of fields that examine human culture and society. Students develop an understanding of major themes in the history of human societies around the globe from the earliest origins to the present. The major offers students a broad, cross-cultural, and humanistic understanding of the past through the study of material culture, supplemented by training in the methods and theories of archaeological field and laboratory work. The major also emphasizes developing critical thinking and analytical skills, as well as an appreciation of the social and ethical responsibilities of those who study the past and its remains. The program offers opportunities for students to participate in archaeological fieldwork and laboratory work through faculty-led projects in the Los Angeles area and abroad. Many of our students are also interested in careers in heritage management and cultural resource management. Students can undertake internships in museums, historical societies, government agencies and private firms. The department has close ties with museums and cultural heritage institutions in the Los Angeles area, including the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County, the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, and the J. Paul Getty Museum.

The Bachelor in Architecture is a five-year professional degree program that integrates general education with a comprehensive curriculum in architectural design, history, theory, building technology, and professional practice. The curriculum emphasizes the development of strong conceptual design abilities and a comprehensive understanding of the cultural, historical, and technological issues of architecture. This program provides students with the intellectual and creative skills to address the complex challenges of the built environment and prepares them for professional careers in architecture and related fields. Students gain a broad understanding of the various aspects of architectural practice, including project management, professional ethics, and client relations, ensuring they are well-prepared for entry into the architectural profession.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Architecture is accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB).

description: Art History majors choose from a wide variety of courses, examining art, architecture, and visual culture from across the globe and throughout history. Through courses that span ancient to contemporary periods and a diverse array of media, students gain an understanding of the historical production, critical reception, and evolving theories of visual art. The curriculum introduces students to a range of methodologies, equipping them with a robust toolkit for analyzing and interpreting images and objects. As a result, Art History majors cultivate their skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, and written and oral communication, preparing them for a range of professional fields. These skills are further strengthened by experiential learning opportunities, including internships at museums and galleries and study abroad programs, which allow students to encounter art firsthand and deepen their knowledge of visual culture. The BA in Art History provides a flexible, interdisciplinary education that fosters intellectual curiosity and prepares students for diverse career paths in the arts and beyond, from graduate study in art history or related fields, to work in museums, galleries, auction houses, non-profit arts organizations, publishing, conservation, historic preservation, teaching, and arts administration.

The universe is presented in terms of astrophysical principles that govern the evolution and structure of planets, stars, galaxies and the universe as a whole. Both observational and theoretical approaches are explored. Courses for non-science majors emphasize the cultural and historical impact of astronomy, as well as the scientific context of current discoveries. Majors in astronomy and astrophysics combine courses in physics and astronomy with an emphasis on research. The program also offers students the opportunity to learn modern astronomical research techniques using the telescopes at the Mount Wilson Observatory.

The Bachelor of Science in Astronautical Engineering program provides a strong foundation in the fundamental engineering disciplines of mathematics, physics, chemistry, materials science, statics, dynamics, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, and electrical circuits. Emphasis is placed on the scientific and technological foundations of modern astronautics. The program also provides a basic understanding of aerodynamics, orbital mechanics, spacecraft dynamics and control, rocket propulsion, and space environment. Laboratory experience is included in the curriculum. All students are required to take a set of core courses and then complete additional units in the areas of astronautics and aerospace electives.

The undergraduate program in biochemistry is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the chemical and biological sciences. The interdisciplinary nature of biochemistry requires students to become proficient in many scientific fields and to integrate this knowledge to solve problems at the interface of chemistry and biology. This preparation provides a foundation for careers in research, medicine and other health professions, biotechnology, and many other fields.

The Bachelor of Science degree in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology provides students with a strong background in the chemistry and biology of living systems. The curriculum offers substantial training in chemistry, mathematics, physics and biology, and then focuses on the molecular aspects of biochemistry and molecular biology. The program is designed to provide excellent preparation for students interested in graduate studies in these and related fields as well as careers in medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, biotechnology, and many other health-related fields. In addition to a rigorous academic curriculum, the program offers opportunities to engage in cutting-edge research in a wide range of fields from structural biology to genomics.
Program name: Bachelor in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology

description: Biomedical engineering is a field dedicated to the application of engineering principles and design concepts to medicine and biology. This field seeks to close the gap between engineering and medicine, combining the design and problem-solving skills of engineering with medical and biological sciences to advance health care treatment, including diagnosis, monitoring, and therapy. The undergraduate curriculum provides a strong foundation in physical, chemical, and biological sciences and mathematics, an introduction to basic engineering principles and design, and a comprehensive exposure to the breadth of biomedical engineering. Through its curriculum, the program prepares students for careers in medical device, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and health care industries, as well as for further graduate studies in biomedical engineering or other professional programs, such as medicine and law.
Program name: Bachelor in Bioengineering and Biomedical Engineering

description: The Bachelor of Science in Global Biotechnology program is an interdisciplinary program that draws faculty from across the university in areas of biology, chemistry, engineering, and business. The program offers students an opportunity to learn about the science, business, and regulatory aspects of biotechnology with emphasis on their global implications. The curriculum includes foundation courses in life sciences and chemistry, advanced courses in biotechnology, and electives covering various aspects of science, business, and policy. Students will be prepared for careers in the biotechnology industry, government, non-profit organizations, or for further graduate studies.

Chemical engineers are concerned with the application of chemical principles to the solution of practical problems. Their work requires an understanding of chemical and physical principles and is unique in its emphasis on process design, particularly involving the transformation of materials. They are responsible for the design and operation of processes for the manufacture of products as diverse as rocket propellants, computer chips, pharmaceuticals, synthetic fibers, plastics, petroleum products, processed foods and beverages, and basic chemicals for industry. The chemical engineer also plays a vital role in medical applications, environmental protection and new materials development. Undergraduate instruction is designed to give the student a strong foundation in chemistry, physics and mathematics and to integrate this material into the engineering sciences through the core chemical engineering courses. The department offers the Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org.

description: The Bachelor of Science degree in chemistry is the appropriate course of study for students contemplating a career in chemistry or a related field (such as biochemistry, chemical physics or materials science), or for students intending to pursue graduate work in chemistry. This degree meets the certification standards of the American Chemical Society.
Accreditation status: Meets the certification standards of the American Chemical Society.

description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Film and Television Production program offers intensive professional training in the cinematic arts combined with a thorough general education. BFA students apply for admission to the program directly from high school. The program provides the conceptual and technical skills necessary for success in the rapidly evolving media environment. Students select one of seven areas of study in which to specialize: producing, writing, directing, cinematography, editing, sound, or animation and digital arts. Students gain a deeper knowledge of the history, theory and aesthetics of moving images. Through a variety of required courses in the liberal arts, students also broaden their understanding of the world, developing the critical thinking skills, humanistic perspective and global awareness necessary for creative expression.
Program name: Bachelor in Cinematography and Video Production

description: Civil engineering is a professional engineering discipline that deals with the design, construction, and maintenance of the physical and naturally built environment, including public works such as roads, bridges, canals, dams, airports, sewerage systems, pipelines, structural components of buildings, and railways. At USC, we offer a comprehensive Bachelor of Science (BS) program in Civil Engineering that prepares students for careers in various fields, including structural, geotechnical, water resources, environmental, transportation, and construction engineering. Our curriculum provides a strong foundation in engineering principles, mathematics, and science, combined with hands-on experience through laboratory work, field trips, and design projects. Our program emphasizes sustainability, resilience, and ethical considerations, preparing graduates to address complex challenges facing society, such as climate change, urbanization, and infrastructure development. With a focus on innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration, our students gain the skills and knowledge necessary to contribute to the advancement of civil engineering and make a positive impact on the world.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science program in Civil Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: Ancient History; Classical Culture; Classical Languages and Literature
description: The Department of Classics offers a Bachelor of Arts degree in Classics. The major is designed to provide students with a broad and flexible education based on the languages and cultures of ancient Greece and Rome, and their lasting influence. It offers three areas of emphasis: Ancient History, Classical Culture, and Classical Languages and Literature. Students are encouraged to consult with the undergraduate advisor in Classics to determine which area of emphasis best suits their interests and professional goals. The major in Classics offers a comprehensive study of the civilizations of Greece and Rome, including their literature, history, philosophy, art, and archaeology. It is designed to provide students with a broad and flexible education based on the languages and cultures of ancient Greece and Rome, and their lasting influence. Students develop critical thinking, analytical, and communication skills applicable to a wide range of careers and graduate studies.

The Cognitive Science major is designed for students interested in the scientific study of the mind, brain and intelligent systems. It provides students with an interdisciplinary understanding of the nature of intelligence through the perspectives and methodologies of psychology, computer science, linguistics and philosophy. Students will explore topics such as perception, memory, reasoning, language, decision-making, artificial intelligence and the neural basis of cognition. The program emphasizes critical thinking, research skills and the integration of knowledge from diverse fields. The curriculum offers a solid foundation in the core areas of cognitive science, along with opportunities for specialization through elective courses.

Communication is arguably the most vital skill in modern society. In a world of digital transformation, social change and global challenges, the need for effective and ethical communicators continues to grow exponentially. The USC Annenberg Bachelor of Arts in Communication program develops students into communication leaders and innovative thinkers, capable of leveraging communication for good and for success across a variety of professional industries and sectors. Annenberg communication majors master foundational theories while also gaining exposure to a diverse range of subject matters relevant to contemporary communication contexts including: health communication, intercultural communication, political communication, organizational communication, social media, entertainment and persuasive communication. Students develop rigorous research skills to analyze complex issues and formulate strategies that impact individuals, institutions, and society at large. Our graduates enter the workforce equipped with the ability to think critically, communicate effectively across multiple platforms, and engage ethically with diverse communities.

Comparative Literature is an interdisciplinary field that investigates literature and culture across national, linguistic, and disciplinary boundaries. The undergraduate major introduces students to global literary traditions, critical methodologies, and translation studies, offering a rigorous humanities education and excellent preparation for graduate study in any humanities discipline or for careers in a wide range of fields.

This degree emphasizes the modern role of mathematics in the sciences, engineering, and data analysis. Students develop a strong analytical foundation and gain extensive experience with advanced mathematical and computational techniques required to solve problems in scientific and engineering disciplines. Students interested in this degree program should apply to the Bachelor of Science in Applied and Computational Mathematics major. For more information, please refer to the USC Catalogue.
Program name: Bachelor in Computational and Applied Mathematics

description: The Bachelor in Computer and Information Sciences program is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous foundation in the theoretical and applied aspects of computer science and information systems. Graduates will be prepared for careers in various computing fields, further graduate studies, and lifelong learning. Upon completion of the Bachelor in Computer and Information Sciences program, students will be able to: Apply fundamental concepts of computer science, including algorithms, data structures, and programming paradigms, to solve complex problems. Design, implement, and evaluate software systems that meet specified requirements. Analyze and interpret data to support decision-making processes. Understand ethical and professional responsibilities in the computing profession. Communicate effectively in technical and non-technical contexts.
Program name: Bachelor in Computer and Information Sciences

description: The Bachelor in Computer Graphics is an interdisciplinary program that emphasizes an advanced knowledge of the aesthetics and practice of computer graphics as they apply to film, television, games, advertising, and scientific visualization. This program will be housed within the Interactive Media and Games Division of the School of Cinematic Arts, in conjunction with the Computer Science Department in the Viterbi School of Engineering. Students are trained for creative, technical, and management positions. This degree offers a common foundation in both areas, combining computer graphics courses with core courses in computer science. Graduates will possess strong artistic and technical skills. They will be prepared to pursue careers across a wide range of industries including visual effects, games, animation, VR/AR, and more.

A bachelor’s degree in computer hardware engineering covers all aspects of modern computer systems. Students learn how to design, build, and test computer hardware, including microprocessors, memory, and peripherals. They also gain a deep understanding of computer architecture, operating systems, and software development. The curriculum includes courses in digital logic design, computer organization, embedded systems, and very large-scale integration (VLSI) design. Graduates are prepared for careers in hardware design, development, and testing, as well as for graduate studies in computer engineering or related fields.

The Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Computer Science is designed to prepare students for careers in the computing industry or for graduate study. This program provides a strong foundation in the theoretical and algorithmic foundations of computer science, as well as hands-on experience in software development. Students gain proficiency in programming languages, data structures, algorithms, operating systems, computer architecture, and software engineering principles. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and innovative design, enabling students to tackle complex computational challenges. Students have the option of pursuing a general computer science curriculum or specializing in various areas through elective courses. The program also provides opportunities for research, internships, and capstone projects, preparing graduates for diverse roles in fields such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, cybersecurity, game development, and more.

The Bachelor of Arts in English offers students an opportunity to study the English literary tradition and its relation to other literary and cultural traditions, as well as the history, theory, and practice of rhetoric and composition. The program provides a foundation in literary history, critical theory, and interdisciplinary approaches to culture. Students learn to read carefully, think critically, and write clearly and persuasively. The Creative Writing Emphasis allows students to gain extensive practice in writing and revising their own fiction, poetry, or nonfiction. Students complete a total of three creative writing workshops and produce a significant portfolio of work in their chosen genre.

The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Dance degree is a four-year, conservatory-style, pre-professional program that fully immerses students in the theory and practice of dance. Through a holistic and rigorous curriculum, students are challenged to explore their artistic, intellectual and creative potential, while gaining an understanding of the historical, theoretical and scientific foundations of the field. Emphasis is placed on developing a comprehensive skill set in ballet, contemporary and hip-hop techniques, improvisation, choreography, performance, dance science and somatic practices. The program culminates in a senior-year capstone project that allows students to integrate their accumulated knowledge and skills to create a final artistic statement. This degree prepares students for professional careers as dancers, choreographers, educators, arts administrators and scholars, as well as for graduate study in dance and related fields.

The Bachelor of Arts degree in Design and Visual Communications is designed to provide students with a broad and interdisciplinary understanding of the theory, history, and practice of design and visual communication. The program integrates various approaches to visual communication, including graphic design, illustration, photography, and new media, within a liberal arts framework. Students will develop critical thinking skills, visual literacy, and practical design abilities, preparing them for careers in fields such as graphic design, advertising, web design, multimedia, and art direction, or for further graduate study.
Program name: Bachelor in Design and Visual Communications

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Drama and Theatre Production is offered by the School of Dramatic Arts. The program gives students a comprehensive liberal arts education within the context of a focused theatre curriculum, enabling them to understand the nature of theatrical experience and the creative process, as well as to develop their own artistic abilities and professional skills. Students completing the degree will demonstrate a broad knowledge of theatre and its literature, history and theory; communicate an understanding of the relationship between their craft and other art forms; and articulate the importance of theatre to society and culture. The program provides the basic theatre production curriculum found in the BFA programs at USC, but within the broader liberal arts foundation of a BA degree.
Program name: Bachelor in Drama and Theatre Production

description: The Bachelor of Science in Earth Sciences is designed for students seeking a strong foundation in geological sciences and preparing for professional careers or graduate studies. The Earth Sciences curriculum offers a wide range of courses in areas such as geology, geophysics, oceanography, paleontology, geochemistry and environmental science. Opportunities exist for individual research with a faculty member. The program has strong ties to the Earth Sciences department, which supports a wide array of research covering modern and ancient processes that shape Earth, other planets, and their environments. The rigorous scientific curriculum, coupled with computational skills, prepares students for advanced studies or careers in fields such as environmental consulting, natural resource management, geological surveying, and risk assessment.

The East Asian Area Studies program provides students with a broad interdisciplinary exposure to the cultures and societies of East Asia (China, Japan, and Korea). The curriculum integrates the study of East Asian languages with study in the humanities and social sciences. The program emphasizes both breadth and depth within the East Asian area, and provides a solid base for students who wish to pursue graduate work or careers in teaching, journalism, business, law, or government service involving East Asia. Courses in the program combine work in East Asian languages with courses in anthropology, art history, comparative literature, economics, geography, history, international relations, philosophy, political science, religion, and sociology. A regional emphasis (China, Japan, or Korea) is normally selected by the student.
Program name: Bachelor in East Asian Area Studies

description: The East Asian Languages and Cultures program is designed for students who desire to gain a deep knowledge of the cultures of East Asia, past and present. It offers the student flexibility in selecting courses that reflect individual interests and goals, while also ensuring exposure to a broad range of knowledge across the various disciplines that constitute the field of East Asian studies.
Program name: Bachelor in East Asian Languages and Cultures

description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures offers a Bachelor of Arts degree in East Asian Languages and Literatures. This major is designed to provide students with comprehensive training in an East Asian language and a broad knowledge of East Asian literary and cultural traditions. Students may concentrate in Chinese, Japanese or Korean. The major combines intensive language study with a sequence of courses on East Asian literature and culture designed to develop critical thinking skills and cultural competency. With their knowledge of an East Asian language and culture, graduates are well prepared for careers in fields such as business, law, international relations, teaching, and translation. The major also provides a strong foundation for advanced graduate study in East Asian languages and cultures.
Program name: Bachelor in East Asian Languages and Literatures

description: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology is the study of interactions among organisms and between organisms and their environment (ecology), and the origins and processes of change in biodiversity over time (evolutionary biology). The Bachelor of Science degree in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology provides students with rigorous training in the fundamentals of ecology, evolutionary biology, and organismal biology, and allows students to specialize in areas of particular interest to them. This program prepares students for graduate studies in ecology, evolution, and organismal biology, and for careers in ecological consulting, conservation, environmental law and policy, and science education. The department provides students with opportunities to participate in original research with faculty, both on campus and at the Wrigley Marine Science Center on Catalina Island.
Program name: Bachelor in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology

description: The department offers a Bachelor of Arts in Economics and two minors, a Minor in Economics and a Minor in Applied Analytics. All three programs provide an in-depth understanding of the principles and applications of economic analysis. Students learn how to analyze economic problems, evaluate policy proposals, and make informed decisions in a variety of contexts, from business to government to international relations. They also develop strong analytical, quantitative and communication skills that are highly valued in the job market and in graduate studies. Students can tailor their program to their interests and career goals by choosing from a wide range of elective courses in various fields of economics, such as behavioral economics, development economics, environmental economics, international economics, public economics and urban economics.

The Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering (BS ECE) program at USC is a four-year curriculum administered by the Ming Hsieh Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. It is ideal for students who wish to pursue a rigorous, accredited program in electrical engineering with the flexibility to specialize in numerous areas ranging from classical electrical engineering to computer engineering to emerging areas in AI, machine learning and quantum computing. The BS ECE curriculum provides a strong foundation in core electrical and computer engineering principles, including circuit analysis, digital systems, electromagnetics, signals and systems, and programming. As you progress, you’ll have the flexibility to choose technical electives and pursue specializations that align with your interests and career goals.
Accreditation status: Accredited by ABET (Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology).

description: English majors at USC study a wide range of literatures in English, from the earliest periods to the most contemporary, with a strong focus on literary history and criticism. The program helps students develop skills in critical reading, analytical thinking, and persuasive writing.
