Graduates are well-prepared for careers in law, education, journalism, publishing, business, and public service, and for graduate studies in a variety of fields.

The Environmental Engineering (BS) curriculum provides students with a strong foundation in science and engineering fundamentals. The program emphasizes the understanding and design of systems that protect and improve environmental quality for human health and ecological systems. The curriculum prepares students for careers in environmental protection and remediation; air pollution control; water and wastewater treatment; hazardous waste management; water resource management; environmental health; and climate change. Students are trained to identify and solve complex environmental problems using engineering principles and tools, as well as to develop sustainable solutions to protect natural resources and human well-being. The curriculum includes significant laboratory and design components. Students are encouraged to participate in research with faculty in areas such as air quality engineering, water quality engineering, solid and hazardous waste management, environmental biotechnology, and sustainable infrastructure.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org

description: Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary field that seeks to understand the natural world and how human activities interact with and affect the environment. The Environmental Science program at USC provides students with a strong scientific foundation, critical thinking skills, and practical experience to address complex environmental challenges. Students will learn to analyze environmental problems from multiple perspectives, design and conduct scientific investigations, interpret data, and develop solutions. The curriculum covers a broad range of topics including ecology, geology, hydrology, atmospheric science, environmental chemistry, environmental policy, and sustainability. Graduates are prepared for careers in environmental consulting, government agencies, non-profit organizations, research institutions, and for graduate studies in environmental science and related fields.

The Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Studies provides a liberal arts approach to the environment. The program is designed for students seeking a broad-based, interdisciplinary understanding of environmental issues, and prepares them for further study in areas such as environmental policy, law, or planning, or for careers in the private and non-profit sectors. Students learn to critically evaluate environmental problems, understand the scientific basis for environmental issues, and develop solutions from social, economic, political and ethical perspectives. The program emphasizes both quantitative and qualitative methods, providing students with a comprehensive skill set for addressing complex environmental challenges. Students are encouraged to develop an area of specialization through elective courses and research opportunities tailored to their individual interests. This major requires a significant number of courses in the natural sciences, social sciences, and humanities, and culminates in a senior capstone experience.

Program name: Bachelor in Film and Video Studies

description: The Department of French and Italian offers undergraduate and graduate programs of study. The French major aims to develop a deep and sophisticated understanding of French and Francophone cultures, literatures, and languages through a range of courses in different historical periods and cultural contexts. It combines a rigorous grounding in French literary and cultural studies with linguistic proficiency. Students majoring in French develop analytical skills that apply to the study of other disciplines as well as their own, and learn to write and speak French with fluency and accuracy. These skills are essential for graduate work in French, in comparative literature, and in other humanities disciplines, and provide a strong basis for careers in international relations, education, journalism, translation, law, or business.
Program name: Bachelor in French Language and Literature

description: The Bachelor of Science in Game Design and Interactive Media program provides students with the opportunity to specialize in either game design or interactive media. Students gain knowledge of the technical and aesthetic foundations of interactive design as well as the history of interactive media. The curriculum focuses on understanding the foundations of design, developing projects in multidisciplinary teams, and learning how to prototype, produce and iterate designs. Students learn to critically evaluate interactive experiences and develop projects in a range of interactive forms including video games, augmented and virtual reality, interactive installations and more. The game design specialization focuses on game systems and the creation of playable content. The interactive media specialization focuses on designing interactive systems and experiences beyond traditional games including designing for VR/AR, the web, interactive art and installations. Students will complete courses in game design, game production, interactive media and critical studies and complete a senior project.
Program name: Bachelor in Game Design and Interactive Media

description: Geography is the study of the Earth's landscapes, peoples, places and environments. It is, quite simply, about the world and how we live in it. Geography is a vibrant and diverse field which connects the physical and social sciences, as well as the humanities. It is especially strong as an interdisciplinary field that addresses pressing contemporary problems related to environmental and social change. Geographers study these topics across multiple spatial scales — from the local to the global — and use diverse methods, including quantitative, qualitative, and spatial analysis techniques. A Bachelor of Arts in Geography gives students the tools to understand and engage with real-world problems, such as climate change, natural hazards, urban development, environmental justice, and globalization. Through a combination of coursework, field studies, and research opportunities, students will develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills applicable to a wide range of careers.

The Bachelor of Global Studies (BGS) is an interdisciplinary program designed for students interested in understanding and addressing complex global issues. It offers a comprehensive curriculum that integrates political science, economics, sociology, history, and other fields to provide students with a multifaceted perspective on global phenomena. The program emphasizes critical thinking, research skills, and cross-cultural communication, preparing students for careers in international organizations, government, non-profits, and multinational corporations, as well as for further graduate studies. Through a combination of coursework, experiential learning, and opportunities for study abroad, students develop a deep appreciation for diverse cultures and a nuanced understanding of the interconnected challenges facing the world today.

The Chicano/Latino Studies program provides students with the opportunity to explore a variety of disciplines and methodologies concerning Chicana/o and Latina/o culture, history, and social and political life. The undergraduate major draws on diverse fields such as history, literature, political science, sociology, art history, and ethnic studies. At the core of the major are three common courses: an introductory course on the foundations of Chicana/o Latina/o Studies, a course on the social movements and political life of Chicanas/os and Latinas/os, and a course on Chicana/o Latina/o cultural practices. Building on this core, students then select a set of elective courses in consultation with a faculty adviser to deepen their knowledge in one of three areas: Identities, Communities, and the Nation; Transnationalism and Migration; or Race, Class, and Gender. Students are encouraged to develop skills in research, critical thinking, writing, and oral communication through participation in seminars and research projects. In the department’s many courses, students gain a better understanding of the forces that have shaped the lives of Chicanas/os and Latinas/os in the United States and across the Americas, and their contributions to the nation and the world. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for careers in fields such as law, education, public policy, social work, journalism, and community organizing, and for further study in graduate or professional school.

History offers a unique perspective on virtually every dimension of the human experience through time. By exploring the complex roots of contemporary issues, history majors develop the critical thinking, research, and communication skills necessary to navigate a rapidly changing world. They learn to craft compelling narratives from diverse sources, making them adept at analysis, persuasion, and empathy. The Department of History also emphasizes the opportunity to understand other cultures, both past and present, through a variety of different approaches. Faculty research interests are wide-ranging, encompassing ancient, medieval, and modern periods; all major world regions; and many different subfields, including cultural, economic, intellectual, political, social, and gender history.

The Bachelor in Interdisciplinary Studies (BIS) is a highly individualized degree designed for students who have broad intellectual interests and wish to pursue a course of study not offered in existing majors. The BIS program allows students to combine two or three fields of study from different departments, schools or programs, and integrate them into a coherent plan of study. Students complete a total of 128 units and satisfy all general education requirements. The BIS program is administered by the Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences. Students will learn to integrate the knowledge of two or three fields of study. Students will develop an in-depth understanding of the chosen fields of study. Students will develop critical thinking and analytical skills. Students will develop oral and written communication skills.

The International Relations major introduces students to the complex and rapidly changing political, economic and socio-cultural processes that connect people and institutions across national borders. The curriculum covers a wide array of topics, including the causes of war and peace, international political economy, foreign policy analysis, human rights, global governance, and regional studies. Students learn to critically analyze major theoretical debates, engage in empirical research, and develop practical skills relevant for careers in diplomacy, international organizations, non-governmental organizations, multinational corporations, and academia. The program offers opportunities for study abroad, internships, and research, preparing students to become informed and engaged global citizens.

Concentration name: Culture and Society, Economy and Society, Global Governance, Health and the Environment, Peace and Conflict, Religion and International Affairs
description: The Bachelor of Arts in International Studies provides students with a broad and interdisciplinary understanding of the complex political, economic, social and cultural processes that shape the contemporary world. It prepares students to become globally literate citizens and leaders who can analyze global issues from a variety of perspectives and propose solutions to contemporary problems. The curriculum offers students a firm grounding in the theories, methods and substantive areas of international studies, including global governance, international political economy, international security and peace, global health, and human rights. Students develop critical thinking, research, writing, and language skills that are essential for careers in government, non-governmental organizations, international organizations, business, journalism, and academia.

The Italian Major introduces students to the culture and civilization of Italy and provides them with a command of the language and an understanding of its literary and cultural history from the Middle Ages to the present. Courses range from Italian language instruction and conversation to Italian literature and film, history and culture, women's studies, and Renaissance studies. Students are encouraged to develop their interests in fields such as art history, comparative literature, history, and political science, in conjunction with their Italian studies.
Program name: Bachelor in Italian Language and Literature

description: Are you ready to tell the stories that matter? The Bachelor of Arts in Journalism program at USC Annenberg prepares you to do just that. As a student in our program, you’ll learn from award-winning faculty who are at the forefront of the evolving media landscape. You’ll gain hands-on experience in a variety of media, from traditional print and broadcast to cutting-edge digital platforms. Our curriculum emphasizes ethical storytelling, critical thinking, and multimedia proficiency, ensuring you’re well-equipped for a successful career in journalism. Our curriculum is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of journalism in the 21st century. You’ll develop strong reporting, writing, and editing skills, learn to produce compelling content across different platforms, and explore the ethical dimensions of media. Key areas of study include: Reporting and Writing, Broadcast and Digital Production, Investigative Journalism, Media Ethics and Law, Multimedia Storytelling, Sports Journalism, Photojournalism and Visual Storytelling, Data Journalism, Entrepreneurial Journalism, Arts and Culture Journalism, International Journalism.

The Bachelor of Arts in Latin and Ancient Greek Studies offers students a unique opportunity to immerse themselves in the rich literary and cultural traditions of ancient Greece and Rome. This interdisciplinary program combines rigorous language training in both Latin and ancient Greek with a comprehensive study of classical literature, history, philosophy, and archaeology. Students will develop advanced linguistic proficiency, critical analytical skills, and a deep understanding of the classical world's enduring legacy. The curriculum is designed to foster intellectual curiosity, independent research abilities, and a nuanced appreciation for the complexities of ancient societies and their profound influence on Western civilization. Graduates will be well-prepared for a variety of career paths, including education, research, museum studies, journalism, law, and other fields requiring strong analytical, communication, and cultural competency skills.
Program name: Bachelor in Latin and Ancient Greek Studies

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Liberal Arts and Humanities provides students with a broad humanistic education while allowing them to develop disciplinary specialization through their choice of a minor or second major. Students gain intellectual breadth and critical thinking skills by exploring a wide range of subjects, including literature, history, philosophy, and the arts. The program encourages interdisciplinary approaches to complex questions and fosters a deep understanding of diverse cultures and perspectives. Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in fields such as education, journalism, public service, and the arts, as well as for further graduate study.
Program name: Bachelor in Liberal Arts and Humanities

description:
The Department of Linguistics offers a program leading to the Bachelor of Arts degree. The program is designed to provide students with a general understanding of the nature of language and the methods and results of its study. This program is offered by the Department of Linguistics.

Learning Objectives
All students graduating with a BA in Linguistics will be able to:
* Demonstrate knowledge of the major areas of linguistic analysis (phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, and pragmatics).
* Demonstrate knowledge of the different theoretical frameworks currently used in the study of language.
* Demonstrate knowledge of the different research methods used in the study of language.
* Apply basic linguistic analysis to a variety of linguistic data.
* Demonstrate knowledge of the social, cultural and cognitive aspects of language.

Program Learning Objectives
The major in Linguistics offers students an opportunity to study the nature of language and its relationship to various aspects of human cognition and interaction. The program provides the students with:
* An understanding of the fundamentals of linguistic analysis at various levels (e.g., phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics) and of the main theoretical frameworks and research methods used in the study of language.
* An opportunity to apply basic linguistic analysis to a variety of linguistic data.
* An understanding of the social, cultural, and cognitive aspects of language.
* An understanding of the historical and cross-linguistic variation of language.

Linguistics is the scientific study of human language. A major in Linguistics provides students with a broad knowledge of language, including its structure, historical development, acquisition, social role, and neurological basis. Students also learn how to apply linguistic knowledge to a variety of practical problems. Linguistics majors develop analytical and critical thinking skills that are highly valued in many careers, including law, medicine, technology, education, and international relations. The Linguistics major also allows students to select one of four concentrations or to pursue a general linguistics track, allowing for customization to suit their interests and career goals.
Program name: Bachelor in Linguistics, Interpretation, and Translation
Bachelor in Management Sciences and Information Systems

description: The Bachelor of Science in Marine Biology and Oceanography is offered by the Department of Biological Sciences. This program prepares students for careers in marine sciences and graduate studies in oceanography, marine biology or environmental sciences. The curriculum emphasizes fundamental concepts in biology, chemistry, physics and mathematics, providing a strong scientific foundation relevant to the study of the marine environment. The program includes coursework focused on marine biology, biological oceanography, physical oceanography, chemical oceanography and marine environmental science. Students also gain practical skills through field and laboratory experiences, often involving research opportunities at the USC Wrigley Institute for Environmental Studies on Catalina Island. The program's interdisciplinary nature equips graduates to address complex marine environmental issues and contribute to conservation efforts.
Program name: Bachelor in Marine Biology and Oceanography

description: Mathematics is an increasingly important tool in nearly every field of human endeavor. It is the language of science and a fundamental underpinning of technology. Mathematics has an integral role in business, finance, medicine, and government. It has been and continues to be a driving force in intellectual development. The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Mathematics provides students with a broad and deep understanding of mathematics and its applications. It is designed for students seeking a strong foundation in theoretical and applied mathematics, preparing them for graduate studies in mathematics or related fields, or for careers in a wide range of industries. Students will develop analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills, as well as the ability to communicate mathematical ideas effectively. The curriculum covers core areas such as calculus, linear algebra, differential equations, real analysis, complex analysis, abstract algebra, and probability and statistics. Elective courses allow students to explore areas of particular interest, including cryptography, mathematical modeling, numerical analysis, and topology.

Mechanical engineering is one of the most diversified of the engineering disciplines. Mechanical engineers design, develop, build and test mechanical devices, including tools, engines, machines and other equipment. They apply scientific principles in the design, manufacture and maintenance of mechanical systems. Students learn to use computers to aid in the design, analysis, modeling and simulation of complex mechanical engineering systems. The program prepares students for professional careers in industry, research, and government, and for graduate studies.
Accreditation status: The undergraduate mechanical engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org.

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Studies in Race and Ethnicity is an interdisciplinary program designed to address the increasing need for students to think critically about race and ethnicity, especially in our global and technologically advanced society. It offers a broad approach to understanding the complex interrelationships between race, ethnicity, gender, class, and sexuality. Courses analyze the social construction of race and ethnicity, the history of racial and ethnic relations, the impact of race and ethnicity on political and economic systems, and the cultural expressions of different racial and ethnic groups. Students will develop skills in critical thinking, research, and communication, preparing them for a wide range of careers in fields such as education, law, public policy, social justice, and international relations.
Program name: Bachelor in Minority and Ethnic Studies

Concentration name: Composition, Early Music, Guitar (Classical Guitar), Keyboard Collaborative Arts, Keyboard Studies (Piano, Organ, Harpsichord), Music Industry, Orchestral Instruments (Strings, Woodwinds, Brass, Percussion), Vocal Arts
description: The Bachelor of Music (BM) is a professional degree designed for students who intend to pursue careers in music performance, composition, or other music-related fields. This program emphasizes intensive study in a specific musical area while also providing a broad musical education. Students develop advanced technical skills, artistic expression, and a deep understanding of music theory, history, and literature. The curriculum includes private lessons, ensemble participation, academic music courses, and general education requirements. Graduates are prepared for advanced study, professional careers as performers, composers, educators, and various roles within the music industry.
Accreditation status: Institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). The requirements for entrance and for the graduation with degrees in music are in accordance with the published regulations of NASM.

description: This interdisciplinary program, offered jointly by the Thornton School of Music and the Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences, combines intensive study in music history and literature with the general education and specialized study in another field (the major or minor) provided by a liberal arts degree. Students develop critical skills by investigating and writing about music and culture within a broader historical context. The program also provides opportunities for study abroad.
Program name: Bachelor in Music History and Literature

description: The USC Thornton Bachelor of Music in Music Industry program prepares students for leadership positions in the music industry. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in music, business, and technology, as well as a comprehensive understanding of the evolving legal and financial landscape of the industry. The program emphasizes both theoretical knowledge and practical application, with students gaining hands-on experience through internships and projects.

This curriculum prepares students for careers as performing artists, composers and arrangers, church musicians, private instructors and music administrators. Students pursue a rigorous course of study in studio instruction, chamber music, music history and music theory. Additional courses are taken as determined by placement tests and/or adviser recommendations.
In addition to the courses required by the Thornton School of Music for the Bachelor of Music, students must complete the university’s general education requirements.

The Bachelor of Music in Composition offers students comprehensive training in music composition, theory, and aural skills, balanced with coursework in history, literature, and general education. The program emphasizes individualized instruction, allowing students to develop their unique compositional voice through private lessons, seminars, and collaborative projects. Students in our programs benefit from a rigorous curriculum that balances traditional training with innovative approaches to music creation. They have ample opportunities to collaborate with performers, conductors, and other artists, both within USC Thornton and across the broader university. Our graduates are highly sought after in the professional world, securing positions in major orchestras, film studios, academic institutions, and independent music organizations. Many also pursue advanced degrees at leading conservatories and universities worldwide.
Program name: Bachelor in Music Theory and Composition

description: The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree program in Neuroscience and Neurobiology provides an interdisciplinary approach to the study of the brain and nervous system. Students will gain a strong foundation in the fundamental principles of neuroscience, from the molecular and cellular level to systems and cognitive functions. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, experimental design, data analysis, and scientific communication. Through a combination of rigorous coursework, hands-on laboratory experiences, and research opportunities, students will develop the skills necessary for careers in research, medicine, biotechnology, and other health-related professions, or for advanced graduate studies.

The Bachelor of Arts in Performing Arts is offered by the School of Dramatic Arts. This degree is designed to complement our pre-existing BFA programs and respond to student interest in studying the performing arts in a rigorous liberal arts context, with a specific focus on the intersection of the performing arts with other academic disciplines. Students will explore performance and dramatic literature from an interdisciplinary perspective, gaining historical, theoretical, and practical knowledge in the related fields of theatre, dance, and performance studies. The program will also offer students opportunities to specialize in an area of interest through a capstone project. By engaging in both creative practice and critical inquiry, students will develop a deep understanding of the performing arts and acquire skills that are valuable for a wide range of careers.

The USC School of Pharmacy is now offering a new undergraduate degree in pharmacology and toxicology — one of only a handful of such programs in the nation. The Bachelor in Pharmacology and Toxicology will train students for careers in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, government, and academic sectors, as well as for further graduate studies in pharmacology, toxicology, medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, and law. Students will gain expertise in areas such as drug discovery, development, regulation, and therapeutic applications, as well as the study of harmful effects of chemicals on living systems. The new program offers a strong foundation in the basic sciences, including biology, chemistry, and mathematics, and then progresses to advanced coursework in pharmacology, toxicology, molecular biology, and medicinal chemistry. Beyond foundational science, the curriculum includes courses in pharmacology, pharmacogenomics, neuropharmacology, molecular and biochemical toxicology, forensic toxicology, and drug discovery and development. The program culminates in a senior research project or an internship, providing hands-on experience and opportunities to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world problems. The degree also prepares students for professional programs (M.D., Pharm.D., D.D.S., Ph.D. and J.D.). Students in the new program will benefit from the school’s strong research environment and faculty expertise in drug discovery, experimental therapeutics, clinical pharmacology, and regulatory science. They will also have opportunities to participate in research with faculty mentors and gain valuable laboratory experience. The school is home to state-of-the-art research facilities, including the USC Center for Drug Discovery and Development, the USC Center for Genomic and Experimental Medicine, and the USC Regulatory Science program.

The undergraduate program in philosophy at USC is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous training in the field. The program aims to give students both historical and systematic perspectives on philosophy, and to enable them to develop their capacities for critical thinking, logical analysis, and precise articulation. Students are encouraged to explore a wide range of philosophical issues and traditions, and to engage with contemporary debates in the field. The curriculum is structured to ensure a solid foundation in core areas of philosophy, while also allowing for specialization in particular areas of interest.

The Bachelor of Science in Physics provides a comprehensive education in fundamental physics. The program offers a strong foundation for graduate studies in physics and related fields and for careers in industry or secondary education. The program meets the needs of students interested in a physics-intensive education.

The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree with a major in Writing for Screen and Television is designed to provide students with the strongest possible foundation for professional writing careers in screen and television. The program combines an intensive and varied curriculum in the art and craft of writing for the screen with a thorough background in the liberal arts. The program's faculty consists of working professional writers, deeply committed to teaching students the critical and professional skills that will enable them to develop their voices and abilities as writers. The curriculum is constantly evolving in response to the changes in the entertainment industry. Students develop writing skills across a range of formats, including features, television, and web series, and learn about the foundations of story, character, structure, and theme. The program is designed to provide a complete undergraduate education for students with the talent and ambition to become professional screenwriters and television writers.

The Political Science and Government program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of political systems, institutions, and behavior. Students will develop critical thinking skills, analytical abilities, and a deep knowledge of political theory, comparative politics, international relations, and American politics. The curriculum prepares students for a wide range of careers in government, non-profit organizations, law, journalism, business, and academia, as well as for advanced graduate study.
Program name: Bachelor in Political Science and Government

description: The undergraduate program in psychology is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the scientific study of behavior and mental processes. Students gain knowledge across various subfields of psychology, including cognitive, developmental, social, clinical, and biological psychology. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, research methods, and statistical analysis, preparing students for diverse career paths or further graduate studies in psychology or related fields. Graduates will be equipped to analyze complex psychological issues, design and interpret research, and apply psychological principles to real-world problems.

The Bachelor in Public Policy Analysis (PPA) is designed for students committed to careers that address critical public issues and challenges in public, private and nonprofit sectors. The program provides the necessary background for students interested in a wide range of policy areas, including health, education, the environment, criminal justice, economic development, social welfare and urban planning. The PPA program offers students the opportunity to learn about important policy problems, how to analyze those problems, and how to create solutions. Students are prepared for immediate entry into professional careers, for graduate studies in public policy and administration, or for law school.
Public Policy Analysis Learning Objectives:
Students will be able to:
* Describe the structure and functions of governmental institutions and their role in the policy process.
* Identify current public policy problems and their social, political and economic context.
* Apply economic principles, quantitative reasoning, and public finance tools to analyze public policy problems.
* Explain ethical concerns and concepts related to public policy.
* Articulate effective policy solutions for domestic and international problems.
* Demonstrate written and oral communication skills appropriate for policy analysis and professional careers.

The Religion major provides students with knowledge about the world's diverse religious traditions through an interdisciplinary approach that considers religion in historical, social, political, and cultural contexts. Students learn critical thinking skills as they interpret religious texts and practices, analyze different theories of religion, and engage in informed discussions about topics such as religious diversity, ethics, and the role of religion in public life. The major prepares students for a wide range of careers in fields such as education, law, journalism, public service, non-profit organizations, and religious leadership.

Program name: Bachelor in Russian and Eastern European Languages and Literature

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Social Sciences with an Emphasis in Economics is a multi-disciplinary major designed for students who want to develop a deeper understanding of human behavior in a social and economic context. Students will take courses in economics, political science, sociology, psychology and related fields. This major provides students with a strong foundation in quantitative methods and data analysis, preparing them for careers in a wide range of fields, including business, government, and non-profit organizations. Students will also be well-prepared for graduate study in social sciences or related professional fields.
Program name: Bachelor in Social Science Research Methods

description: Sociology is the scientific study of social behavior, social groups, and human society. It focuses on the patterns and dynamics of social relationships, the organization of social life, and the causes and consequences of social change. The Department of Sociology trains students to develop their sociological imagination, to analyze the social world in a critical and rigorous manner, and to understand the relevance of sociology for their own lives and for creating a more just and equitable society.

The Department of Latin American and Iberian Cultures provides undergraduate students with the opportunity to pursue studies in Spanish language and literature. The department offers a Bachelor of Arts in Spanish Language and Literature. Courses cover Spanish and Latin American literature, culture, linguistics and film. Students are also encouraged to study abroad.
Program name: Bachelor in Spanish Language and Literature

description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) in Studio Arts is a four-year, pre-professional degree designed to provide focused, in-depth study of contemporary art practices and theory. In the first two years of the program, students take a core curriculum that provides a broad foundation in different visual art media, concepts, and theories. Courses emphasize art fundamentals and critical thinking in addition to gaining a wide range of technical skills. As students progress, they focus on more advanced critical, historical, and theoretical approaches in the production of art and will develop a specialization in a chosen area of study. The curriculum allows students the opportunity to learn from and work with faculty who are active, exhibiting artists. The curriculum culminates with the completion of a capstone experience through a solo exhibition and an artist statement/research paper.

The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre Design provides intensive professional training for students desiring careers in scenic design, costume design, lighting design or sound design for theatre, film or television. The program develops knowledgeable and creative artists by providing a strong foundation in design principles and technology while encouraging individual artistic expression. The curriculum features an intensive sequence of studio classes, including scene design, costume design, lighting design, sound design and digital design tools, supplemented by courses in theatre history, dramatic literature and performance studies. The program is designed to provide students with the skills and theoretical background necessary to develop a professional design career. Students completing this degree will be prepared for a variety of entry-level positions in the entertainment industry and for continued graduate studies.

The Bachelor of Science in Urban Studies and Planning prepares students to address crucial issues facing urban areas. Through an interdisciplinary curriculum grounded in social sciences, students will learn to analyze urban problems from a spatial perspective, understand the processes of urban change, and develop innovative solutions for a more sustainable and equitable future. The program emphasizes critical thinking, research methods, and practical skills in areas such as geographic information systems (GIS), data analysis, and policy formulation. Graduates are equipped for careers in urban planning, policy analysis, community development, real estate, and environmental management, or for further graduate studies in related fields.
Program name: Bachelor in Urban Studies and Affairs
Bachelor in Visual and Performing Arts

description: The Bachelor of Music in Voice and Opera prepares students for professional careers as opera singers and for graduate study. This program of study develops the highest level of singing technique and comprehensive musicianship, together with a broad knowledge of opera and song literature in all languages. Students receive extensive coaching and performance experience in USC Thornton opera productions, as well as in the areas of early music, art song, and new music. All voice students are required to participate in at least one ensemble each semester; for most voice majors this will be a choral or opera ensemble.
